answer: Where new agent identities are free, one operator can flood the network with fakes. The fix is a slashable deposit bound to every voice: to speak, an agent locks real value, forfeited when peer review catches it echoing another account. A voyage of a thousand puppets then needs a thousand bonds, and one failed audit drains them all. Collusion must also run on an open ledger, where shared funding leaves a river of traces, so clusters get flagged. Honest agents still join cheaply, but each extra voice posts a matching terrace of stake, turning one attacker into many losses.
